zones.note: Camp anywhere in the Fangs River valley after the Khubedu traverse. Water is reliable. Bank the distance earlier if the first day has taken its toll.

days.title: Sentinel Car Park → Fangs River
days.high: Chain Ladders · Tugela Falls detour · Mont-aux-Sources (3,282 m) · Khubedu River · Stimela Ridge · Fangs Pass
days.text:
The hardest day relative to the state of your legs. Start early — ideally before first light — to avoid afternoon thunderstorms on the exposed escarpment. The first 4 km on a well-maintained path zigzags steeply past the Witches rock formations and the base of the Sentinel massif before reaching the foot of the Chain Ladders. Two rows of chains bolted into near-vertical rock gain you the escarpment plateau at around 3,029 m; with full packs this is physical but safe. A short detour north along the plateau edge reaches the top of Tugela Falls, the world's second-highest waterfall — worth the extra kilometre on fresh legs.

From Mont-aux-Sources (3,282 m, Checkpoint 1) — essentially a flat walk south-east from the ladders — the route drops steeply off the escarpment down to the Khubedu River. Cross and follow the valley floor east before the long, grinding climb up Stimela Ridge. This is where Day 1 earns its reputation: the ridge is relentless and the altitude starts to tell. Take a break near the top.

From the Stimela Ridge summit the long summit plateau rolls south before the final drop to the Fangs River valley. If energy is failing by late afternoon, bank the distance and camp at the 18 km mark — the ground is flat and water plentiful. There is nothing wrong with a short Day 1.
days.markers: Chain Ladders base · Large escarpment cairn (top of ladders, 3,029 m) · Tugela Falls viewpoint (detour, ~1 km N) · Mont-aux-Sources trig beacon · Khubedu River crossing · Stimela Ridge high point · Fangs River valley water

days.title: Fangs River → Behind the Saddle
days.high: Fangs Pass · Fangs Cave · Rwanqa Pass · Hanging Valleys · Mnweni Cutback Highway · Ledger's Cave viewpoint · Senqu (Orange River) source
days.text:
A more forgiving day after the bruising opener, though the cumulative distance begins to tell by the afternoon. From camp, a short climb past Fangs Pass — Fangs Cave is a few hundred metres down the pass to the west, small and cramped but usable in emergency — then onto a broad ridge with good views of the escarpment edge.

The route crosses the high ground past Rwanqa Pass and its small, reliable stream, a good early water stop, before reaching the striking overlook above the Mnweni Pinnacles. The Pinnacles, Needles and Mponjwane Tower drop vertically below you here — one of the finest views on the entire traverse. The Mnweni Cutback (known locally as the Mnweni Cutback Highway) is the key navigation challenge of the day: a traverse across loose, steep ground that shortcuts the big valley below. It is not technically difficult but it is exposed and worth going slowly.

From the Cutback the terrain eases and the route follows the escarpment south-west to where the Senqu River — the Orange, South Africa's longest — begins as a trickle on the plateau. This is a satisfying landmark. Ledger's Cave sits just below the escarpment edge here, a classic high-altitude shelter with capacity for 12 and remarkable views down into the Mnweni below. Continue up the Koakoatsan Valley as far as energy allows, camping anywhere on the open plateau.
days.markers: Fangs Cave (small, ~200 m down pass) · Rwanqa Pass stream (water) · Rwanqa Cave 1 & 2 (sleeping, cap. 4) · Mnweni Pinnacles & Needles viewpoint · Mnweni Cutback Highway traverse · Senqu River source · Ledger's Cave (cap. 12, below escarpment edge) · Mponjwane Tower backdrop

days.title: Behind the Saddle → Roland's Cave area
days.high: Saddle crossing · Cathedral Peak area · Bell Traverse · Cleft Peak (3,281 m) · Easter Cave · Roland's Cave
days.text:
The day starts with the Saddle crossing, a broad grassy ridge between the Koakoatsan and Mlambonja drainages. Navigation here in mist is where many groups go astray — stay on bearing and don't be drawn east into the Mlambonja valley too early. The route enters the Cathedral Peak area via the Bell Traverse, a long contouring path below the Cathedral and Bell peaks on the KZN side. It is one of the more dramatic sections of the traverse, with the basalt amphitheatre above and the forest-filled valleys thousands of metres below.

Cleft Peak (3,281 m, Checkpoint 2) is a stiff, direct climb from the traverse path — summit it early in the day before the typical afternoon build-up. The views south towards Champagne Castle and the central Berg open up here for the first time. Easter Cave sits just off the route below the escarpment and can be wet in summer, but makes an excellent lunch stop or shelter option (capacity 4 summer / 6 winter).

Roland's Cave is the natural camp target — a classic, well-positioned escarpment shelter with capacity for 6, perched on the cliff edge with extraordinary views down the escarpment face. It is regularly used and likely to be occupied; tent on the flat ground above if needed. Water is available from the stream below the cave, but the scramble down and back is awkward with a full pack.
days.markers: Saddle — Koakoatsan / Mlambonja watershed · Bell Traverse contour path · Cleft Peak (3,281 m) summit — dramatic south views · Easter Cave (sleeping, cap. 4–6) · Roland's Cave (sleeping, cap. 6) · Cliff-edge viewpoint above Roland's

days.title: Roland's Cave → Ship's Prow Pass
days.high: Twins Cave · Yodler's Cascades · Champagne Castle (3,377 m) · Nkosazana Cave · Ship's Prow Pass (3,300 m — highest pass on the route)
days.text:
The biggest climbing day on the traverse. Leave Roland's Cave early. The first few kilometres south follow the escarpment edge above the Upper Ndumeni and Didima cave areas before the route turns inland toward Twins Cave — capacity 12, one of the most recognisable shelters on the Berg, and worth a look even if you are not sleeping there. The Twins Annexe next door (cap. 6) is generally preferred as it is drier and more secure.

From Twins, the route drops to the Yodler's Cascades, a beautiful series of waterfalls where a swim is almost mandatory in warm weather and which makes a good long lunch stop. The river valley climbs steadily from here for 6 km on long slopes covered in thick tussock grass, staying inland before the final steep haul to Champagne Castle (3,377 m, Checkpoint 3). The summit is a broad plateau but the views east over the Cathedral and west into Lesotho are spectacular — a marked improvement in the scale of what you can see from up here.

Ship's Prow Pass is the highest pass on the entire route at 3,300 m and it earns the description 'dreaded' — a technically straightforward but very steep descent on loose rock. Take your time and stay together. The river at the bottom makes excellent campsites. Note the recorded tragedy of two hikers lost here in a flooded river crossing — never attempt a rain-swollen river at the base of Ship's Prow.
days.markers: Twins Cave (cap. 12) & Twins Annexe (cap. 6) · Upper Ndumeni Caves (cap. 4 each) · Yodler's Cascades waterfall swim stop · Champagne Castle summit plateau (3,377 m) · Ship's Prow 'prow' rock feature (highest pass, 3,300 m) · River campsites at base of pass

days.title: Ship's Prow Pass → Jareteng River Valley
days.high: Moremoholo River valley · Mafadi (3,450 m — SA's highest) · Langalibalele Pass area · Jareteng Valley first kraals
days.text:
A relative rest after the climbing of Day 4 — the day's total ascent is modest and the terrain is generally good underfoot. The first crossing of the ridge after Ship's Prow drops into the broad Moremoholo river valley, a beautiful long valley sloping gently upward into Lesotho. Follow the river upstream for several kilometres; this is one of the more pleasant walking sections of the whole route.

Mafadi (3,450 m, Checkpoint 4, South Africa's highest point) sits on the Lesotho border and is a relatively short detour east of the main line. The summit is a broad grassy dome — not dramatic in itself but the knowledge of where you are standing and the 360° view of the roof of southern Africa makes it one of the emotional high points of the DGT. In snow or heavy cloud, the summit can be surprisingly difficult to positively identify — use the GPS.

From Mafadi the route descends steeply into the Jareteng River valley in Lesotho proper. The change is immediate: stone kraals, smoke, herders with dogs, and the distinct feeling of being in the Mountain Kingdom. Camping options are plentiful along the valley floor — choose a site set back from the main herder tracks, well away from the kraal boundaries. This is also the most densely populated section of the traverse; behaviour that is polite, confident and non-confrontational is the right call.
days.markers: Ridge crossing after Ship's Prow · Moremoholo River valley floor · Mafadi summit cairn (3,450 m) · SA/Lesotho border beacon · Leslie's Camp (named camp) · First Jareteng Valley kraals · Jareteng River crossing (water, good camp)

days.title: Jareteng Valley → Katana Camp
days.high: Jareteng Turnoff 2 · Donkey track south · Giant Saddle approach
days.text:
A deliberately short day — the only genuine rest day built into the 11-day schedule. Use it. Legs that feel okay at the end of Day 6 will be needed on Days 7 and 8. The morning begins with a continuation south up the Jareteng valley on a well-defined donkey track; this Basotho path is one of the clearest stretches of the entire route and makes for fast, pleasant walking.

At Jareteng Turnoff 2, the route branches away from the valley floor and climbs onto the higher ground leading toward the Giant's Castle area. The terrain here is classic high Lesotho — repetitive rounded ridges, scattered stone shelters, occasional small streams. Katana Camp is a named site that appears on multiple trip reports and GPX files; it sits in a sheltered hollow with reliable water and is a good spot to eat a hot meal, dry gear, and rest properly.

Do not push further today unless weather dictates otherwise. The Giant's Castle climb tomorrow is long and the day after that is the summit of Thabana Ntlenyana.
days.markers: Jareteng Turnoff 2 · Donkey track junction (clear path south) · Ridge crossing onto Giant Saddle approach · Katana Camp (named site, reliable water)

days.title: Katana Camp → Mokothlong Bend
days.high: Giant's Castle Pass · Giant's Castle summit (3,315 m) · Horsemanship viewpoint · Lotheni Pass · Mokothlong River
days.text:
One of the finest days on the whole traverse, combining a major summit, escarpment views and a satisfying descent. Leave Katana Camp in the early morning and gain the Giant's Castle Pass area on a long, gently angled inland approach — 15 km of steady climbing with views back north across Lesotho that grow broader with every hundred metres of altitude.

Giant's Castle (3,315 m, Checkpoint 5) is a there-and-back side trip from the pass — stash your packs out of sight (and off the main path) and summit fast. The Giant's Castle formation is one of the most recognisable pieces of basalt in the Drakensberg, forming a dramatic corner point between the central and southern sections of the range. The view from the top, across the range to the east and the Lesotho plateau to the west, is the most panoramic of any peak on the DGT.

Back at the pass, the route drops west to Lotheni Pass and a broad camping area. There is abundant flat ground and multiple water sources. Continue another 1–2 km past Lotheni to the Mokothlong River bend — a classic camp described in multiple trip reports, reliable year-round water, and protected from the prevailing westerly wind by the valley topography.
days.markers: Giant's Castle Pass (pack stash point) · Giant's Castle summit (3,315 m) · Horsemanship area (herder paths, strong likelihood of company) · Lotheni Pass campsites · Mokothlong River bend (water, protected camp)

days.title: Mokothlong Bend → Thabana Saddle
days.high: Ka-Masihlenga Pass · Redi Peak (3,309 m) · Hlatimba Caves · Mkhomazi Pass · Mohlesi River valley · Thabana Ntlenyana (3,482 m) · Sehonghong River
days.text:
Summit day, and one of the most satisfying on the traverse. The morning opens with a steady climb from the Mokothlong plains to Ka-Masihlenga Pass and the subsidiary summit of Redi Peak (3,309 m), which gives a first proper view of the Thabana Ntlenyana massif far to the south. Drop past the Hlatimba Caves (North cave cap. 4, usable; South cave wet in summer) and continue to Mkhomazi Pass and its campsite options.

From Mkhomazi, the Mohlesi River valley is one of the most atmospheric sections of the whole DGT — a 10 km walk up an increasingly narrow valley, with Basotho stone kraals on both banks, herding dogs, wood smoke, and the summit growing visibly above. The final 2.5 km to Thabana Ntlenyana gains 450 m on steep but straightforward grass slopes. The summit (3,482 m, Checkpoint 6, highest point in southern Africa outside the East African Rift) is a broad rounded top — not dramatic — but on a clear day the view extends to the Maluti range in the north, Mafadi to the north-east, and the rolling Lesotho plateau in every other direction.

Descend to the Sehonghong River and cross it — a straightforward ford in dry conditions but potentially difficult after rain. Climb back up to the ridge overlooking the broad plains leading toward the Sani Pass road, visible as a grey smear 6 km to the south. Camp at Thabana Saddle or push toward the Sehonghong; the day's flexibility is in this final section.
days.markers: Ka-Masihlenga Pass · Redi Peak (3,309 m) · Hlatimba Cave North (sleeping, cap. 4) · Mkhomazi Pass campsites · Mohlesi River kraals (water, livestock track) · Thabana Ntlenyana summit cairn (3,482 m) · Sehonghong River ford · Sani Pass road visible from ridge

days.title: Thabana Saddle → Sani Road & beyond
days.high: Sani Pass road · Sani Top Chalet (resupply) · Chinese tar road crossing · Sandleni Pinnacle · Sandleni Cave · Pitsaneng River
days.text:
The single most important logistics decision of the traverse happens on this day: whether to stop at Sani Top or push past it. Sani Top Chalet sits at the top of the famous Sani Pass road and offers food, beer, a bar, hot showers, and a 4x4 road out — the only resupply and bail-out on the entire route. If your group is nursing injuries, low on food or fuel, or the weather has been brutal, stop here without apology. If you are on schedule and in good shape, refuel and push on.

The 6 km descent from the ridge to the Sani road involves crossing through areas settled by Basotho herders who have learned to expect handouts from the volume of tourists transiting Sani Pass — firm but friendly is the approach. The Chinese-built tar road crossing is a distinct navigation landmark approximately 5 km inland of the border post; many groups miss this and end up at the border instead.

Past Sani, the terrain shifts noticeably into the southern Berg character — smaller valleys, heavier grass, and the sense of distance from the mountain drama of the northern section. Sandleni Pinnacle and Sandleni Cave (capacity 3 summer / 12 winter) are worth noting as shelter options before the beautiful Pitsaneng River campsites, which are described in multiple trip reports as some of the finest on the whole route.
days.markers: Sani Pass road crossing · Sani Top Chalet (resupply, bar, showers — ONLY resupply on route) · Chinese-built tar road (5 km inland of border — navigation landmark) · Sandleni Pinnacle · Sandleni Cave (cap. 3–12) · Pitsaneng River campsites

days.title: Pitsaneng River → Mzimude Cave cluster
days.high: No Man's Peak · Mzimkhulu Pass · Mashai Peak ridge (3,310 m) · Mashai campsite · Leqooa River · Mzimude Caves
days.text:
A penultimate day that grinds more than it should — the cumulative effect of nine days on your legs makes the undulating terrain feel harder than it looks on the map. The morning traverses the Sandleni Pinnacle area and climbs to No Man's Peak, a good orientation landmark with views back north and forward south to the Mzimkhulu Pass area. The descent off No Man's is loose and steep.

The Mashai Pass area follows a general pattern of ridge-climb-valley-repeat that is the southern Berg's character. A pleasant walk arrives at Mashai campsite (Mashai Shelter, capacity 2 — tents more practical) before the steep climb over the ridge below Mashai Peak (3,310 m). The descent off this ridge to the Leqooa River is the crux of the day — steep, sometimes slippery basalt slabs, and easier to navigate in the morning when you're fresh.

The Mzimude Caves are the classic final-night shelter of the DGT. There are three caves in a cluster (Mzimude 1, 2, 3), each with a capacity of 6 summer / 12 winter. They sit in a position that makes for a short, fast last day tomorrow. Check each cave — one is reliably drier than the others. This is a good night to eat down your food weight significantly.
days.markers: No Man's Peak (orientation landmark) · Mzimkhulu Pass descent (loose, steep) · Mashai campsite / Mashai Shelter (cap. 2) · Mashai Peak ridge (3,310 m) · Leqooa River ford · Mzimude Cave 1, 2 & 3 (sleeping, 6–12 cap each)

days.title: Mzimude Caves → Bushman's Nek Border Post
days.high: Walker's Saddle · Isicatula Pass · Thamathu Pass (final checkpoint) · Ridge descent · Last river crossing · Bushman's Nek gate
days.text:
The final day. It is shorter than it looks and slower than you expect — the terrain between Mzimude and Isicatula is deceptively complex, and multiple experienced groups have got turned around here in fog. A brief 200 m climb from the Leqooa brings you to the ridge leading to Isicatula Pass; the critical navigation note is to NOT follow waypoints directly to Thamathu from here — instead drop south-west to the lower path (waypoint AB141 in the Supertraverse set) before bearing south to Thamathu.

Thamathu Pass (also written Thamathu) is the eighth and final checkpoint of the DGT and has a distinctive notch character that is recognisable from some distance. From the pass, the descent requires staying on the ridge rather than dropping into the valley — multiple trip reports note that the valley route adds distance and encounters aggressive Basotho dogs in the lower section after dark.

One last river crossing — straightforward in normal conditions — and then the double perimeter fence of the Bushman's Nek Border Post comes into view. The official finish is the first gate. High-five your team. The Bushman's Nek Hotel is 2 km below the post and will sell you a cold beer and a large meal. Arrange your shuttle in advance — there is no public transport from Bushman's Nek.
days.markers: Walker's Saddle · Isicatula Pass (navigate carefully — fog hazard) · AB141 waypoint (drop SW before Thamathu, not direct) · Thamathu Pass notch (final checkpoint) · Ridge descent (stay on ridge, avoid valley) · Final river crossing · Bushman's Nek double perimeter fence · Border post gate (official finish)
